validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/OWNERSHIP all confirmed independently, this is a well-documented, real, operating pipeline. It is the offshore ('marine') natural gas pipeline running from the Texas/Mexico border near Brownsville, TX across the Gulf of Mexico to Tuxpan, Veracruz, built and operated as a 60%/40% TC Energy (formerly TransCanada) / IEnova (Sempra's Mexican unit) joint venture named 'Infraestructura Marina del Golfo' (IMG). Confirmed by TC Energy's own 2022 Annual Report asset table (pdftotext-extracted p.35 of the PDF: 'Sur de Texas 770 km ... Offshore pipeline that transports natural gas from the U.S./Mexican border near Brownsville, Texas, to Mexican power plants in Altamira, Tamaulipas and Tuxpan, Veracruz ... 60%' -- note the PDF is 19MB/300+pp and url_verifier's extractor does not reach this page, a documented false-negative for large PDFs per the tool's own header comment; I downloaded it directly and ran pdftotext -layout to confirm the text is really there), IEnova/Sempra's own corporate page (semprainfrastructure.com: 'Gasoducto Sur de Texas-Tuxpan ... Built in collaboration with TC Energia ... 800 km pipeline and a 100,000 HP compression station. It is the largest private marine pipeline ever built in Mexico'), TC Energia's own Spanish asset page (tcenergia.com/activos/sistema-sur-de-texas-tuxpan/: JV between TC Energia and IEnova, 'IMG'), and independent trade press (offshore-technology.com: TransCanada 60% / IEnova 40%, JV named Infraestructura Marina del Golfo, 25-year build-own-operate contract with CFE). GEM's Operator field 'TC Energy, IEnova' is a reasonable shorthand for this JV -- the actual operating entity is IMG, not named separately in GEM's schema; noting this as a minor attribution nuance, not an error. STATUS='operating' confirmed by Natural Gas Intelligence (naturalgasintel.com, Oct 2, 2019 article, fetched and read in full): '...just days after the 2.6 Bcf/d Sur de Texas-Tuxpan natural gas pipeline went into operation...' -- this also independently corroborates Capacity=2.6 Bcf/d/2600 MMcf/d. START YEAR=2019 is corroborated by that same NGI article (operational as of early Oct 2019) plus two Mexican outlets whose headlines both date the in-service event to September 17, 2019 (Milenio: 'Gasoducto marino Sur de Texas-Tuxpan inicia operaciones'; El Financiero: 'Gasoducto Sur de Texas-Tuxpan inicia operaciones luego del acuerdo entre IEnova y Gobierno') -- both blocked on fetch (Milenio 403, El Financiero 500; access failures, not confirmed deletions, so not cited directly but corroborate via their own headlines/dates recorded in the wiki's citation metadata). LOCATION: TC Energy's own asset table lists interconnects at BOTH Altamira, Tamaulipas AND Tuxpan, Veracruz -- GEM's EndLocation='Tuxpan' captures the pipeline's namesake/primary terminus and is not an error, just incomplete (worth a note that the system also reaches Altamira). FUEL='Gas' trivially confirmed (natural gas pipeline throughout all sources). No duplicate found against the 45-row Texas-gas roster -- no other row describes a Texas-to-Mexico offshore/Gulf pipeline terminating in Veracruz; NET Mexico Gas Pipeline (P0224, Nueces County) and Nueva Era Pipeline (P0290, ?->Nuevo Leon) are geographically and physically distinct corridors. Classification (gas transmission trunk, not gathering/feeder) is correct. Of the 23 harvested wiki citations for this row I opened/attempted 16: 9 confirmed live with matching content (tcenergy.com project page, tcenergy 2022 annual report PDF, proyectosmexico.gob.mx, offshore-technology.com, semprainfrastructure.com, tcenergia.com asset page, tcenergia.com 2016 contract-award news, naturalgasintel.com 'CFE charges ahead'), 2 confirmed dead (404: naturalgasintel.com/articles/117196-... and pgjonline.com/2017/05/26/... -- access failures now permanent per HTTP 404, not cited), 3 blocked/transient (Milenio 403, El Financiero 500, IEnova investor-relations PDF 403 -- access failures, NOT treated as deletions), 1 navigation surface skipped (ijglobal.com/data/search-projects, a live search page not an article), 1 off-topic (chron.com article is about the unrelated Valley Crossing Pipeline, P0276 -- likely a stray citation on the wiki page, not used). 7 of 23 citations (FracTracker map, IEnova asset-map image, and 5 further NaturalGasIntel/MexicoBusinessNews articles on later CFE pipeline expansions) were not opened; they read as later-stage market-context pieces about OTHER planned pipelines, not additional facts about P0257 itself, but are flagged here as unexhausted pool items per the worklist-not-lookup-table rule.

validity.recommendation: Stage refs for Length, Diameter, and Capacity cells as-is; no value change needed.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC (length/diameter/capacity) confirmed by 2+ genuinely independent sources each, materially agreeing with GEM's staged values. LENGTH (GEM 770 km): TC Energy's own 2022 Annual Report asset table states 770 km exactly; Mexico's federal investment-project registry proyectosmexico.gob.mx (CFE's own tender/contract page for this project) states 772 km -- a 0.3% difference, immaterial, both agree closely with GEM. (Two other sources, Sempra Infrastructure and offshore-technology.com, round to ~800 km/497 mi -- a looser approximation but not a contradiction; noting the spread for completeness.) DIAMETER (GEM 42 in): confirmed exactly by TWO independent sources -- proyectosmexico.gob.mx ('772 km y 42 pulgadas de diametro') and offshore-technology.com ('42 inches'), plus TC Energia's own Spanish asset page (42 inches) as a third, non-independent-of-TC-Energy corroboration. CAPACITY (GEM 2600 MMcf/d / 2.6 Bcf/d): confirmed by proyectosmexico.gob.mx ('capacidad de 2,600 millones de pies cubicos diarios (MMPCD)'), offshore-technology.com ('2.6 billion cubic feet of natural gas a day'), and NaturalGasIntel's Oct 2019 article ('the 2.6 Bcf/d Sur de Texas-Tuxpan natural gas pipeline'). All three specs are corroborated by at least one source fully independent of TC Energy/IEnova (the Mexican federal government's own project registry, and/or an independent trade press outlet), satisfying the >=2-independent bar. No material disagreement found on length, diameter, or capacity.

validity.recommendation: Flag SegmentCost for Update review -- do not treat as fully corroborated; consider annotating in ResearcherNotes that reported project cost has varied materially ($2.1B est. at 2016 contract award -> $2.73B CFE tender/'Solvente Ganadora' contract value -> $3.1B per Offshore Technology, which is the figure matching GEM exactly). Likely explanation is cost escalation/scope difference between the original 2015-16 tender estimate and final capital cost, but this is inference, not confirmed by a document that states both figures and reconciles them.
validity.researcher_notes: SEGMENTCOST (GEM $3,100,000,000 USD): this is the one figure I could NOT cleanly corroborate to >=2 independent, mutually-agreeing sources. offshore-technology.com states 'Total Investment: $3.1 billion' -- an exact match to GEM's figure, and it is an independent trade-press source. However, two other sources in the pipeline's own citation trail report materially different, earlier cost figures for what appears to be the SAME project: (1) TC Energia's own June 2016 contract-award announcement (tcenergia.com) headlines '$2,100 millones de dolares' as the total project cost, with the body text saying TransCanada 'espera invertir aproximadamente $1,300 millones de dolares' (~60% share of $2.1B, consistent with the 60/40 split); (2) Mexico's proyectosmexico.gob.mx project page records a winning-bid/contract value ('Solvente Ganadora') of $2,727,080,379.47 USD (~$2.73B) from the original 2015-16 CFE tender. So there are three different total-cost figures on record for this one project: ~$2.1B (2016 announcement) / ~$2.73B (CFE tender contract value) / $3.1B (Offshore Technology's 'total investment', which matches GEM). These could plausibly reflect different stages (2015-16 tender/contract value vs. final realized capital cost by completion in 2019, given construction delays pushed in-service from a planned late-2018 to September 2019), but I found no single document that names more than one of these figures and reconciles them, so I am not certifying this as resolved. GEM's number is directly matched by exactly one independent source; the two lower figures are both closer to each other in time (2015-2016) and could represent the pre-construction estimate. Recommend Update treat SegmentCost as medium/low confidence pending a source that ties the $3.1B figure explicitly to actual/final project cost (e.g. an IEnova or TC Energy capex disclosure) rather than an announced or tendered estimate.
